facts.basis: the flag is the whole content of the readback; no second source is consulted for dead

facts.claim: A living agent whose PlayerLocomotion current state is Downed reports downed.
facts.basis: PLOC_Downed is a state of the locomotion machine (dump.cs 539315), entered and exited by the machine itself
facts.inference: the state is the game's own downed state; the observation does not decide when it is entered

facts.claim: Health and its ceiling travel as `hp.<current>` and `hp.max.<maximum>` string tags.
facts.basis: RuntimeEntitySnapshot (ForgeRuntime/Framework/EntityObservationContracts.cs) has no health field; the shared snapshot shape is owned by the framework contract and was not changed here

facts.claim: Reads run only where the identity module already tracks lives, i.e. the host.
facts.basis: PlayerIdentityModule.CanObserve requires SNet.IsMaster; the host is the only plan executor, so a client-side reader has no consumer

facts.claim: The entity number in `gtfo.player:<n>` is the module's first-recorded order, not the native slot.
facts.basis: PlayerIdentityModule numbers lives as they are recorded (dump.cs 650689 is the only slot read); the observer publishes the slot separately as the `player.slot-<n>` tag, so a client UI never has to read a slot out of an entity ID
facts.consequence: the two numbers coincide on a full host session only by accident; nothing in the snapshot depends on them agreeing

facts.claim: A player life advertises the one recipient capability this provider serves, `health.heal`, exactly where the reader can also serve it: a verified receiver on a living agent.
facts.basis: the player health receiver (evidence/player-health.json) commits through Dam_SyncedDamageBase::SendSetHealth, and the native receive path refuses an owner that is not alive, so a dead player or one without a readable damage base advertises nothing
facts.consequence: a downed player still advertises it, because Alive stays true in this model; the observer claims the heal it can accept, never a revive

unverified.question: Does PlayerAgent.Alive stay true for the whole downed state, and only clear at the dead transition?
unverified.why: the flag is read from a metadata signature; no game execution, no input data and no runtime order were observed

unverified.question: Is Dam_PlayerDamageBase.Owner always the owning PlayerAgent at runtime?
unverified.why: the field exists in metadata; the observation treats a mismatch as 'no health' rather than guessing

unverified.question: What Health value does the damage base hold while downed or dead?
unverified.why: no runtime sample; the health tags are published whenever the receiver is consistent, including for a downed player

unverified.question: Do PlayerAgent.PlayerSlotIndex and SNet_Player.PlayerSlotIndex always agree?
unverified.why: the equality is treated as an identity check; a disagreement is refused as no snapshot, which is deliberately conservative

unverified.question: Which recipient capability a player must advertise for a heal action to accept it.
unverified.why: resolved after this observation: the player health receiver now exists (`PlayerHealthReceiver`, `forge.module.gtfo.map.binding.heal` binding `forge.action.combat.heal`), and the snapshot advertises `health.heal` for a verified receiver on a living agent (see the `health-heal-receiver` fact above)
unverified.followUp: the enemy receiver is unchanged and still refuses `gtfo.player` references; whether a plan's heal step pins the Map binding for a player target is the website's binding-selection question, not this provider's

unverified.question: The `forge.selector.target.players` query binding: which relation anchors it, and what `empty` does.
unverified.why: `relation` is a required structural parameter whose graph carries no anchor (self/source/owner/instigator/event-target), and `empty` is read without a runtime skip or fail path to apply it to
unverified.decision: the binding answers `relation: ally` only, from the module's recorded lives, and reads `empty` without acting on it; the other relation names are refused with `relation-unsupported` instead of guessing an anchor; caller-side policy is what applies `empty`
unverified.followUp: a subject-carrying selector graph must exist before `self`/`hostile`/`neutral` can be answered from an anchor

unverified.question: That a plan's `query` step reaches this binding through the kernel's own dispatch, not only through a direct call.
unverified.why: the framework now builds the session (`RuntimeKernel.Control.cs` EvaluateStep constructs the EvaluationContext with BeginQuery, and `RuntimePlan.cs` accepts a `query` node whose binding role is `observe` and that declares a world port), so the binding resolves and is dispatchable; no Map test drives a whole plan dispatch, and no game run happened, so the end-to-end path is unexecuted here
unverified.note: the evaluator takes no world read of its own: it publishes the identities the module records, and every snapshot read is charged to the consuming step through RuntimeQuerySession and RuntimeKernel.InspectEntities, which is where the query budget applies
unverified.followUp: drive one plan whose query step binds `forge.module.gtfo.map.binding.target.players` and confirm the session and the budget once a game-side consumer exists
